title: Knowledge Check 3: Lessons 11–15
description: Pooled check over Lessons 11–15 of the Salesforce Architect series. Score 80% or higher to unlock the cert prep exam.

questions.question: Per the lesson “Security Architecture: The Sharing Model, OWD, Role Hierarchy, Sharing Rules, and Manual Sharing”, what is the central focus?
options: Who can see a given record? The four record-level controls that answer it: org-wide defaults, the role hierarchy, sharing rules, and manual sharing. How they la…
A history of the technology and its vendors
A review of unrelated productivity tools
A summary of corporate policy rules
questions.explanation: The lesson is centered on: Who can see a given record? The four record-level controls that answer it: org-wide defaults, the role hierarchy, sharing rules, and manual sharing. How they layer, how they only ever open access, and why 'most permissive wins' is the whole game.

questions.question: Which statement best reflects the lesson’s guidance?
options: This lesson is the deep dive every architect needs on the four record-level controls: org-wide defaults (OWD), the role hierarchy, sharing rules, and manual sharing.
Your integration can write a record to Salesforce, but that says nothing about who can see it.
Object permissions say a user may touch Accounts; the sharing model says which Accounts.
Get the sharing model wrong and the result is either a sales team that can't see its own territory or, worse, a field user who can see everyone's compensation.
questions.explanation: Your integration can write a record to Salesforce, but that says nothing about who can see it.

questions.question: Per the lesson “Data Architecture: Data Model Design, Common Data Model Patterns, and Data Skew”, what is the central focus?
options: Data is the load-bearing wall of every org. Designing a data model that scales means deciding where each relationship lives, recognizing the recurring shapes th…
A history of the technology and its vendors
A review of unrelated productivity tools
A summary of corporate policy rules
questions.explanation: The lesson is centered on: Data is the load-bearing wall of every org. Designing a data model that scales means deciding where each relationship lives, recognizing the recurring shapes that solve real problems, and keeping the load off any single parent record or owner. This lesson covers data model design, the common patterns (one-to-many, many-to-many, hierarchical, and data tiering), and the three data skews that quietly break performance.

questions.explanation: The lesson is centered on: The data side of AI systems. Embeddings, vector databases, chunking, and why the modeling discipline from a Salesforce data model (records, relationships, source of truth, scale) carries over unchanged when the storage engine becomes a vector store. Includes a worked example of a RAG knowledge base, a pgvector walkthrough, and the Data Cloud vector database connection.
